newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel sharply higher against basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel sharply higher against basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose sharply against the basket of currencies on Wednesday following the recent rise of the dollar against the mark, dealers said.

"The shekel remains stable against the dollar at 3.4 to 3.5 shekels per dollar despite the rise of the dollar against the mark abroad. This leads to a sharp rise of the shekel against the basket," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
The dollar surged on Wednesday to near eight-year highs of 1.89 marks per dollar. The U.S. currency has risen over 20 percent on the mark this year.
"Israeli investors are only intrested in the dollar and they buy and sell it regardless of what the dollar does overseas," he said. "This keeps pushing the basket downwards."
He added that volume continues to be low and the market is quiet.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5410 shekels compared with 3.5440 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7506 against 3.7645 on Tuesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9683 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.9913 on Tuesday, and against the mark at 1.8762 shekels compared with 1.8851 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5400 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
